title: Canonical coefficient-duality maps on a small ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], where $\mathcal O$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. Use its category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived tensor obtained from the total tensor complex after K-flat resolutions [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and $H(A,B)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(A,B)$ obtained from K-injective resolutions [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Regard $\mathcal O$ as a complex concentrated in degree zero and write $A^\vee=H(A,\mathcal O)$. For arbitrary $A,B\in D(\mathcal O)$ there are canonical morphisms
$$e_{A,B}:B\otimes_{\mathcal O}^{\mathbf L}A^\vee\longrightarrow H(A,B),\qquad b_A:A\longrightarrow H(A^\vee,\mathcal O).$$
The first is natural contravariantly in $A$ and covariantly in $B$; the second is natural covariantly in $A$. The map $e_{A,B}$ is the derived internal-composition map $H(\mathcal O,B)\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(A,\mathcal O)\to H(A,B)$ after the canonical identification $B\cong H(\mathcal O,B)$. The map $b_A$ is the transpose of coefficient evaluation with its tensor factors exchanged by the Koszul symmetry. Both maps are normalized on ordinary representatives as follows. Let $E,F$ be complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules representing $A,B$, with $F$ K-flat, put $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])$, and suppose that $D$ is K-flat and that the maps $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal O[0]))$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal I^\bullet(F))$ induced by the fixed K-injective resolutions of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] are quasi-isomorphisms, so that $D$ represents $A^\vee$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$ represents $H(A,B)$. Then, under these identifications and the comparison $Q\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\cong B\otimes^{\mathbf L}A^\vee$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], $e_{A,B}$ is the image of the chain map $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes D)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,F)$ sending $y\otimes\phi\in F^p\otimes D^q$ to the degree-$(p+q)$ map $x\mapsto y\,\phi(x)$, with no sign. Similarly, for any complex $E$ representing $A$ such that, with $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal O[0])$, the maps $D\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal O[0]))$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,\mathcal O[0])\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal O[0]))$ are quasi-isomorphisms (no flatness required), $b_A$ is, under these identifications, the image of the chain map $E\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,\mathcal O[0])$, $x\mapsto\bigl(\phi\mapsto(-1)^{|x||\phi|}\phi(x)\bigr)$ for homogeneous $x,\phi$. Hom complexes carry the differential $d(f)=d_{\mathrm{target}}f-(-1)^{\deg f}f d_{\mathrm{source}}$ [def-pur-hom-complex] and total tensor complexes the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. For every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$, restriction to the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] takes both maps to the corresponding canonical maps on that site, under the canonical restriction comparisons for derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and derived internal Hom [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]; slice restriction is the exact module pullback of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. No perfectness, boundedness or invertibility of either displayed map is asserted.
